statement.text:
Let n be a positive integer. For a finite group K and an automorphism
                                                                        n−1
ϕ of K of order dividing n, let Xn,ϕ (K) := {x ∈ K | xxϕ · · · xϕ            = 1}. Let
cn be the supremum of the ratios |Xn,ϕ (H)|/|H| over all finite groups H and their
automorphisms ϕ ∈ Aut(H) such that ϕn = id and Xn,ϕ (H) ̸= H.
   (a) Let n > 1 be a positive integer such that cd < 1 for all prime power divisors d
of n. Is it true that cn < 1?
   (b) For a finite group G and a positive integer n, the generalized Hughes–Thompson
subgroup is defined as Hn (G) = ⟨x ∈ G | xn ̸= 1⟩. Suppose that n is a positive integer
for which there is a positive integer kn depending only on n such that |G : Hn (G)| ⩽ kn
for all finite groups G with Hn (G) ̸= 1. Is it true that then cn < 1? This question is
open even when n ⩾ 5 is prime.                               A. Abdollahi, M. S. Malekan
